transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, uh, I hope I'm not wasting your time—it's probably nothing major, really. 

But... well, I guess what brings me in is I've been having this little issue with driving. Specifically, uh, high bridges. It sounds kind of silly for a grown man to admit, I know, but I keep finding myself planning my whole day around just... not having to drive over them. I'll take the long way around just to avoid them. And, you know, if I absolutely can't get around it, I'll do it, but I just sort of white-knuckle the steering wheel the whole way across. 

Is that... does that make sense? I just thought maybe I should get some advice on how to handle it, if that's the sort of thing you help with here.
Do you find yourself avoiding or feeling anxious in situations other than driving over high bridges?

No, no, not really. I mean, I'm generally a pretty laid-back guy, you know? I don't get worked up about much else. It's really just the bridges. 

I mean, sure, everyone gets a little nervous sometimes, right? Like maybe if I'm up really high on a ladder cleaning the gutters, I might feel a little uneasy, but nothing out of the ordinary. I can still do it. It's not like the driving thing. 

I hope that's... is that the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Is your anxiety when driving over high bridges related to the fear of heights or the fear of something happening while driving, such as crashing or losing control?

Well, it's... it's not so much a general heights thing, I don't think. It's really just the driving part, specifically on those big bridges. 

I mean, logically, I know those bridges over the bay are built fine, right? Engineers know what they're doing, and folks drive over them every single day without any issues. I tell myself that. But... when I get near one, my mind just sort of plays tricks on me. It acts like the car could just... go right over the side. Like I might lose control or something terrible could happen. 

I know it sounds a bit irrational when I say it out loud. I really try not to let it get to me. Does that make sense, though? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you.
Have you ever experienced a sudden, intense fear or discomfort while driving over a high bridge that reached a peak within minutes?

Well, I wouldn't say it's like a full-blown panic attack or anything like that. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. But... yeah, I guess I do get pretty uncomfortable pretty fast. 

It's usually right as soon as I see the bridge coming up in the distance. My chest gets a little tight, and my hands start sweating on the wheel. I just sort of lock up and stare straight ahead, like I just have to make it to the other side as fast as I can. It peaks pretty quickly, I suppose, right as I'm getting onto the bridge. 

But I always get across! I just white-knuckle it. Is that... is that the kind of sudden feeling you meant? I hope I'm answering that right.
Does the anxiety occur only when you are driving over the high bridge yourself, or does it also happen when you are a passenger?

Oh, um... no, actually. It's really just when I'm the one behind the wheel. 

If, say, my wife is driving, or if I'm catching a ride with a buddy from work, I'm mostly fine. I mean, I might look out the window and think, 'Wow, we're up pretty high,' but I don't get that tight chest or anything. Because they're the ones in control, you know? I don't have to worry about... well, about me making a mistake or doing something wrong. I just sit back and let them handle it. 

I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means it's not too serious, right? Is that the kind of detail you needed to know?
Does the anxiety you experience when driving over high bridges have anything to do with feeling like you're in control of the vehicle?

Yeah, I think so. It's... it's definitely tied to that feeling of being the one in charge of the car. 

Like I was saying, when someone else is driving, I just don't have that same worry. But when it's me, it's like... I just get this flash of, 'What if I mess up?' Even though I'm a very safe driver! I really am. I've never had an accident or anything like that. It's just this silly thought that pops up when I'm up that high, that maybe I'll lose control of the wheel. 

I know it doesn't make total sense, and I try not to make a big deal out of it. I just grip the wheel a little tighter and get through it. Does that... does that sound like what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think your anxiety would decrease if you were driving over the bridge in a vehicle that you felt was extremely safe or stable, such as a large truck?

Um, you know, I've never actually thought about that before. I've only ever driven my sedan over them. 

I guess... maybe? If I was in something bigger, like a big truck, maybe I'd feel a bit more planted on the road. But I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't want to guess and give you the wrong answer. 

Do you think that would make a difference? I mean, whatever you think makes the most sense is probably right. I just haven't had the chance to try it out. I hope it's okay that I don't have a better answer for you on that one.
Would your anxiety decrease if you were in control of a different vehicle or mode of transportation that requires similar control, such as a boat?

Oh, wow, um... a boat? I've actually never driven a boat, so I'm really not sure. 

I mean, I'd like to think I'd be okay? A boat seems pretty safe, right? You're just out on the water, not really up high or anything. So maybe I wouldn't have that same weird feeling. But honestly, I'm just guessing here. I don't want to mislead you or give you a bad answer. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making this too difficult by not knowing for sure. I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Would you feel anxious if you were in control of a different vehicle, like a bike or an ATV, in a situation that required similar control to driving over a high bridge?

Oh, a bike or an ATV? Hmm... I haven't ridden a bike in a really long time, and I don't think I've ever actually been on an ATV. So I really couldn't say for sure. 

I'd like to think I wouldn't make a fuss about it, you know? I try to be pretty level-headed about most things. But since I haven't actually been in that exact situation, I'd just be guessing, and I really don't want to give you false information. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm striking out with these questions about other vehicles. I really want to give you the information you need to do your job. Is it okay that I just don't know the answer to that one? I hope I'm not messing up your evaluation.
Would you feel anxious if you were driving a car on a winding mountain road with no guardrails?

Um, a mountain road with no guardrails? Oh, gosh... I think... I think I'd probably be a little nervous, just because, you know, there aren't any guardrails. I think anyone would be a little cautious in that situation, right? 

But honestly, I haven't driven on a road like that in years. We don't really have mountains around here. So I'm not entirely sure how I'd react now. I'd probably just take it slow and steady, try not to make a big deal out of it. 

I hope that's a better answer for you. I feel like I'm finally giving you something you can use, even if it's just a little bit. Does that sound like a normal reaction to you? I just want to make sure I'm on the right track here.
Would you feel anxious if you were in control of a plane as a pilot?

Oh, wow, flying a plane? Um... I've never done that either, so I really can't say for sure. 

I imagine anyone would be a little nervous flying a plane for the first time, right? But I'd like to think I'd handle it okay. I try to be pretty dependable and follow instructions well. I just wouldn't want to mess anything up. 

But since I've never been in a cockpit, I really don't have a good answer for you. I'm sorry, I know you're trying to figure this all out, and I keep saying I don't know. Is it helpful at all that I'm trying to imagine these scenarios for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to do your assessment.
Would you feel anxious if you were driving a car on a straight road with no obstacles, but someone else was controlling the accelerator?

Oh, um... driving but someone else is doing the gas pedal? Honestly, I don't think I've ever been in a situation quite like that either. I mean, maybe like driver's ed way back when I was a teenager? But even then, I don't really remember it bothering me too much.

I'd like to think I'd be fine. I'm usually pretty easygoing about letting other people take the lead if they know what they're doing. I wouldn't want to be a control freak or anything, you know? As long as it was a straight road and there wasn't any traffic, I think I'd just trust the other person and try not to be a bother. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm giving you another "I don't know" answer. Am I being too difficult? I really am trying to think these through for you. I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and helping you out. Is it okay that I'm not totally sure about these hypothetical situations?
Would you feel anxious if you were in control of a train or a similar vehicle that requires operation but is on a fixed path?

Um, driving a train? Gosh, I... I really don't know. I've never worked on a railroad or anything like that. 

I suppose if it's on a fixed track, that takes a lot of the pressure off, right? You just sort of... go forward and stop when you're supposed to. I think I'd be okay with that. I'd just follow the rules and try to do a good job. I definitely wouldn't want to cause any delays or mess up the schedule for anyone. 

I feel terrible, I keep giving you these wishy-washy answers because I just haven't done any of these things. I really hope I'm not frustrating you. Am I giving you the kind of information you need for your notes? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and being helpful.
Would you feel anxious if you were in control of a boat on a large body of water?

Um, driving a boat? Wow, you have some really interesting questions. I've actually never driven a boat either. 

I think... well, on a big open lake or something, where there's plenty of space? I'd probably be fine. I'm usually pretty careful, and I wouldn't want to get in anyone else's way or cause an accident. I'd just take it slow and make sure I was doing exactly what I was supposed to do. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like a broken record here with all these things I've never done. I really hope I'm not wasting your time with all these guesses. Is this still useful for your evaluation? I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.
Would you feel anxious if you were in control of a bicycle on a high bridge?

Um, a bicycle on a high bridge? Oh, wow. I... well, to be completely honest, that one might actually bother me a little bit. 

It's not the bicycle part, really. It's... well, it's the bridge. I know it sounds a bit silly, and I know those big bridges over the bay are built perfectly fine. I mean, folks drive over them every single day without a second thought, right? But... when I get near one, even in a car, my mind just sort of acts like the car could go right over the side. 

So, being on a bicycle? Out in the open like that? I think I'd probably be pretty nervous. I'd hate to hold up traffic or be a nuisance to anyone else trying to get across because I was going too slow or feeling panicky. 

I hope that doesn't sound too ridiculous. I know it's not very logical. Is it okay that I get a little anxious about things like that? I'm really trying to give you the best answers I can.
Would your anxiety about driving over high bridges decrease if you were driving a vehicle with a higher center of gravity, such as a large truck or SUV?

Um, a bigger vehicle? Like a truck or an SUV? Gosh, I... I don't think that would help, honestly. 

I think, if anything, being higher up might actually make it a tiny bit worse. Just because... well, you're closer to the edge, right? Or at least it feels that way. I'd probably just be worrying even more about tipping over or something, even though I know those vehicles are perfectly safe and people drive them all the time. 

I'd just want to stay in my lane and not cause any trouble for the other drivers. I wouldn't want to be the guy going ten miles an hour in a big truck and making everyone angry. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit irrational. I hope I'm not coming across as too difficult or complicated. Does that answer make sense for what you're looking for?
Would your anxiety about being on a high bridge decrease if you were walking across it instead of driving?

Um, walking across? Oh, my. I... I think that might actually be the worst option for me, to be perfectly honest. 

I know it's probably silly, because pedestrians cross bridges all the time, right? But... just the thought of being out there, completely exposed, with nothing between me and the edge but a little railing... my stomach just kind of drops thinking about it. I'd be so worried about getting dizzy or tripping and somehow going over. 

And I'd hate to be a bother to anyone else walking, you know? Like if I had to stop and catch my breath or if I was clinging to the side and getting in people's way. I always try to be mindful of others. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just giving you all these complicated, anxious answers about bridges. I really hope I'm not sounding too neurotic. Is this the kind of information you need? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Would you feel anxious if you were in control of a vehicle that doesn't require constant steering, such as a train, but still allows you to control its movement?

Um, a train? Oh, well... I've never actually driven a train, of course. But... if I were in control of one, and it was on a high bridge? 

I... well, I suppose it might be a tiny bit better than a car, just because, like you said, I wouldn't have to steer. It's on tracks, so it can't really veer off the side, right? I know they're incredibly heavy and secure. 

But... I think I'd still be a little uneasy. Just being up that high, looking down... it's just the height and the water down below that gets to me. Even if I knew intellectually that the train wasn't going anywhere, my mind would still play those little tricks on me. 

I'd probably just want to get across as quickly as possible without causing any disruption to the schedule. I wouldn't want to be the conductor who slows down the whole route just because he's a little jumpy, you know? 

I hope that makes sense. I'm trying to imagine it the best I can for you. Am I answering these questions okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of details.
Would your anxiety about high bridges be present if you were a passenger in a car driven by someone else over the same bridge?

Um, a passenger? Well, yes, I... I think I'd still be a little nervous. 

It's maybe a tiny bit easier than driving myself, just because I don't have to worry about making a mistake at the wheel and causing an accident that hurts someone else. But... I still get that tight feeling in my chest just looking out the window and seeing how high up we are. 

I try really hard not to show it, though. I don't want to be a nuisance to whoever is driving or make them feel like they have to slow down or change their route just for me. I usually just kind of grip the door handle quietly and look straight ahead until we're across. 

I'm sorry, I know it's probably frustrating to hear that nothing really makes it go away completely. I'm trying my best to be a good patient and give you the right answers. Is it okay that I still feel anxious even when I'm not the one driving?
